name: Logistics & Supply Chain
tagline: Shipments, on-time delivery, transit time, freight cost, exceptions and fill rate across carriers and lanes
description: TMS and carrier exports, courier and 3PL MIS reports at AWB level, freight invoices, order-fulfilment files and truck trip sheets, including Indian-market fields such as AWB, LR, EDD, NDR and RTO.

fields.label: Shipment / AWB ID
fields.description: Identifies each shipment; repeats on every line when the file lists items or packages.

subDomains.name: Shipments & deliveries
subDomains.description: One row per shipment, consignment or AWB (or per package within it) with dates, carrier and status.

subDomains.name: Order fulfilment
subDomains.description: One row per order or order line with ordered and shipped quantities and fulfilment dates.

subDomains.name: Fleet trips
subDomains.description: One row per truck trip or load with vehicle, distance, weight and cost.

kpis.name: Shipments
kpis.definition: Number of distinct shipments dispatched in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct shipment IDs

variants.label: Distinct order IDs
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each order is counted as one shipment.

variants.label: Row count
variants.caveat: No shipment or order ID, so every row is counted as one shipment. Check the grain.

kpis.name: On-time delivery rate
kpis.definition: Share of delivered shipments that arrived on or before the promised date.
kpis.formula: Shipments delivered on or before the promised calendar day ÷ delivered shipments with a promised date

variants.label: Delivery day ≤ promised day, per shipment
Delivery date ≤ promised date, per row
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is one shipment and dates are compared including the time of day.

variants.label: Actual ≤ planned transit days, per row
variants.caveat: No promised date, so actual transit days are compared with planned transit days, one row per shipment.

variants.label: Not flagged late, per row
variants.caveat: No delivery or promised dates, so the late-delivery flag in the file is used.

benchmark.note: Indicative: many shippers target 95% or better; acceptable levels depend on mode, season and the service promise.

pitfalls: Definitions differ: some measure against the customer's requested date, others against the carrier's committed date.
Shipments still in transit are excluded until delivered, so the latest periods can fall as late shipments arrive.

kpis.name: Average transit time
kpis.definition: Average calendar days from dispatch to delivery, for delivered shipments.
kpis.formula: Σ (delivery date − ship date) ÷ delivered shipments, one value per shipment

variants.label: Transit-days column, per shipment
variants.caveat: No delivery date, so the transit-days column is used as supplied.

variants.label: Delivery − ship date, per row
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is treated as one shipment.

variants.label: Transit-days column, per row
variants.caveat: Uses the transit-days column as supplied, one row per shipment.

pitfalls: Mix matters: more air or short-haul shipments lower the average without any carrier improving.
A few very slow shipments move the average; check the transit-time distribution.

kpis.name: Freight cost
kpis.definition: Total amount spent moving goods in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of freight cost

kpis.name: Cost per shipment
kpis.definition: Average freight cost of a shipment.
kpis.formula: Freight cost ÷ shipments (ratio of sums)
pitfalls: Driven by shipment size and distance: heavier or longer-haul loads raise it without any loss of efficiency.

kpis.name: Perfect order rate
kpis.definition: Share of completed shipments that were delivered on time with no exception, damage or return.
kpis.formula: Delivered on or before the promised day with a clean delivered status ÷ shipments no longer in transit (cancelled excluded)

variants.label: On time and delivered cleanly ÷ completed, per shipment
On time and delivered cleanly ÷ completed, per row
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is one shipment and dates are compared including the time of day.

variants.label: Not late and delivered cleanly ÷ completed, per row
variants.caveat: No promised date, so timeliness comes from the late-delivery flag.

pitfalls: Only the final status is visible: an exception that was resolved and then delivered on time still counts as perfect.
Delivered shipments with no promised date count as imperfect, so missing promise dates pull the rate down.

kpis.name: Cost per kg
kpis.definition: Freight cost per kilogram moved.
kpis.formula: Σ freight cost ÷ Σ weight, on rows that have both
pitfalls: Uses the weight column as supplied: actual and chargeable (volumetric) weight give different answers.
Light parcels always cost more per kg; compare within a weight band.

kpis.name: Exception rate
kpis.definition: Share of shipments that hit a delivery exception such as a failed attempt, hold or misroute.
kpis.formula: Shipments with an exception status ÷ shipments (cancelled excluded)

variants.label: Exception rows ÷ rows
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is treated as one shipment.

pitfalls: Status files show only the latest status: exceptions that were later resolved and delivered are not counted.

kpis.name: Damage & loss rate
kpis.definition: Share of shipments damaged or lost in transit.
kpis.formula: Shipments with a damaged or lost status ÷ shipments (cancelled excluded)

variants.label: Damaged or lost rows ÷ rows
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is treated as one shipment.

kpis.name: Return / RTO rate
kpis.definition: Share of shipments that came back to the shipper undelivered or refused.
kpis.formula: Shipments with a returned or RTO status ÷ shipments (cancelled excluded)

variants.label: Returned rows ÷ rows
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is treated as one shipment.

pitfalls: Cash-on-delivery and remote destinations usually return more; compare like-for-like before blaming a carrier.

kpis.name: Fill rate
kpis.definition: Share of ordered units that were shipped.
kpis.formula: Σ shipped quantity ÷ Σ ordered quantity, on lines that have both

benchmark.note: Indicative target range in distribution; the right level depends on the industry and service promise.

pitfalls: Lines with no shipped quantity yet are left out, so open orders do not drag the rate down; a shipped quantity of 0 does count.

kpis.name: Average order cycle time
kpis.definition: Average calendar days from order to final delivery.
kpis.formula: Σ (last delivery date − order date) ÷ delivered orders, one value per order

variants.label: Delivery − order date, per shipment
variants.caveat: No order ID, so each shipment is treated as one order.

variants.label: Delivery − order date, per row
variants.caveat: No order or shipment ID, so each row is treated as one order.

kpis.name: Freight cost % of value
kpis.definition: Freight cost as a share of the value of the goods shipped.
kpis.formula: Σ freight cost ÷ Σ shipment value, on rows that have both
pitfalls: Cheap, bulky goods always carry a high freight share; compare within a product category.

kpis.name: First-attempt delivery rate
kpis.definition: Share of delivered shipments that were delivered on the first attempt.
kpis.formula: Delivered shipments with at most one attempt ÷ delivered shipments with attempts recorded

variants.label: One-attempt rows ÷ delivered rows
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is treated as one shipment.

kpis.name: Cost per km
kpis.definition: Freight or trip cost per kilometre driven.
kpis.formula: Σ cost ÷ Σ distance, on rows that have both
pitfalls: If distance is recorded per shipment on a shared trip, the same kilometres are counted more than once.

kpis.name: Vehicle load factor
kpis.definition: Share of vehicle weight capacity actually used on trips.
kpis.formula: Σ weight carried ÷ Σ trip capacity, counting each trip's capacity once

variants.label: Weight ÷ capacity, per row
variants.caveat: No trip ID, so each row is treated as one trip with its own capacity.

pitfalls: Weight is only one constraint: bulky, light loads fill a truck by volume long before weight.

kpis.name: Trips
kpis.definition: Number of distinct trips or loads run in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct trip IDs

variants.label: Row count
variants.caveat: No trip ID, so every row is counted as one trip.

kpis.name: Delivered shipments
kpis.definition: Shipments delivered to the consignee.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct shipments with a delivered status

variants.label: Has a delivery date
variants.caveat: No delivered status, so shipments with a delivery date count as delivered.

variants.label: Delivered rows
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each delivered row is counted as one shipment.

kpis.name: Late shipments
kpis.definition: Shipments delivered after the promised date.
kpis.formula: Count of shipments whose delivery day is later than the promised day

variants.label: Delivery day > promised day, per shipment
Delivery date > promised date, per row
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is one shipment and dates are compared including the time of day.

variants.label: Rows flagged late
variants.caveat: No delivery or promised dates, so the late-delivery flag in the file is used.

kpis.name: Average delay when late
kpis.definition: For shipments that arrived late, the average number of days past the promised date.
kpis.formula: Average of (delivery day − promised day) over late shipments, one value per shipment

variants.label: Days late, per late row
variants.caveat: No shipment ID, so each row is one shipment; same-day deliveries later than a timed promise count as 0 days late.

kpis.name: Average time to dispatch
kpis.definition: Average calendar days from order to dispatch.
kpis.formula: Average of (ship date − order date), one value per order

variants.label: Ship − order date, per row
variants.caveat: No order ID, so each row is treated as one order.

kpis.name: Order line fill rate
kpis.definition: Share of order lines shipped in full.
kpis.formula: Lines with shipped quantity ≥ ordered quantity ÷ lines with both quantities
pitfalls: Stricter than the unit fill rate: one short unit fails the whole line.

kpis.name: Weight shipped
kpis.definition: Total kilograms moved in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of weight
pitfalls: If the file repeats a shipment's weight on every package or item line, the total is overstated.

charts.title: Shipments over time
charts.reason: Shipments per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: On-time delivery rate
charts.reason: A rate over time is recomputed per period from delivered shipments and drawn as a line, never summed.

charts.title: Freight cost over time
charts.reason: One additive amount over a continuous time axis: a line with a soft fill shows the shape and the volume.

charts.title: Shipments by carrier
charts.reason: One count compared across named carriers: sorted horizontal bars keep names readable. Top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Freight cost by mode
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a handful of modes or service levels: a donut of at most six slices shows the split at a glance.

charts.title: On-time rate by carrier
charts.reason: A rate compared across carriers: sorted bars of the recomputed on-time rate, carriers with under 30 rows hidden as too small.

charts.title: Carrier cost vs on-time rate
charts.reason: Two measures per carrier: a scatter shows which carriers are both cheap and reliable without a dual axis.

charts.title: Transit time distribution
charts.reason: Transit times are skewed by a slow tail: a histogram shows how many shipments take how long, which the average hides.

charts.title: Late shipments by reason (Pareto)
charts.reason: A few causes usually explain most delays: columns per reason with the cumulative share as a line on the same 0–100% axis show what to fix first.

charts.title: Fill rate by warehouse
charts.reason: A rate compared across warehouses: sorted bars of the recomputed fill rate, warehouses with under 30 lines hidden.

charts.title: Load factor by vehicle
charts.reason: Capacity use compared across vehicles: sorted bars of the recomputed load factor, vehicles with under 20 rows hidden.

charts.title: Lane scorecard
charts.reason: Several service and cost measures per lane side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

pitfalls: On-time rate depends on the promise: a carrier that quotes generous delivery dates looks reliable. Read it alongside transit time.
Recent periods are incomplete: shipments still in transit have no delivery date yet, so on-time rate, transit time and returns shift as they close.
Cost per shipment and per kg depend on the mix of lanes, modes and weights; compare carriers on the same lanes before ranking them (Simpson's paradox).
Item or package-level files repeat the shipment on every line: count shipments with DISTINCT IDs and check that shipment-level weights and costs are not repeated on each line.
Carriers, lanes and warehouses with few shipments swing wildly; treat rates from fewer than about 30 shipments as noise.
On-time is judged by calendar day when a shipment ID is available, so a delivery late in the evening of the promised day still counts as on time.
